does: Cuts the flesh of a fish away from its bones in whole, clean pieces.
how: Lay the fish flat. Cut behind the head and the fin, down to the backbone.
Turn the blade flat and run it along the backbone toward the tail in long strokes, keeping it against the bones.
Lift the fillet away, turn the fish over and do the same on the other side.
Run a finger down each fillet and pull out the small bones it finds.
Keep the bones and the head for a stock.

cues.text: A whole fillet with smooth edges, and a skeleton with almost no flesh left on it.
The blade rides on the bones the whole way.

mistakes.mistake: Sawing with a dull or stiff knife, which tears the flesh.
mistakes.fix: Use a sharp, flexible blade and long, light strokes.

mistakes.mistake: Lifting the blade away from the bones, which leaves flesh behind.
mistakes.fix: Keep the flat of the blade pressed against the backbone.
